stages.text: ReleaseSteward asks a practical rollout question: can old and new clients still share the same database? This is the working local SQLite harness. GitLab Duo and GitLab pipelines have not been verified.
Start with a one release rename from status to state. The migration succeeds, but only three of nine checks pass. The old client cannot read its column. A green migration is not enough.

Choose the compatible strategy. This executes the authored expand and backfill fixture. A model is not generating a repair. All nine checks now pass, including reads, writes and inserts in both directions.
Open the technical evidence to inspect the executed SQL, schema and reproducible hashes. These results come from actual database execution.
Export saves the actual JSON report for review. Local reports do not invent a pipeline URL.
Now add a required column without a default. Existing rows cause the migration to fail. The remaining checks are skipped, rather than presented as executed success.

Every audit is isolated in memory. These are controlled fixtures, not production certification. Actual GitLab Duo execution, platform evidence and the final submission video remain pending. A human retains the release decision.

ALTER TABLE work_orders ADD COLUMN priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal'
CREATE TRIGGER sync_status AFTER UPDATE OF status ON work_orders WHEN NEW.state IS NOT NEW.status BEGIN UPDATE work_orders SET state = NEW.status WHERE id = NEW.id; END
CREATE TRIGGER sync_state AFTER UPDATE OF state ON work_orders WHEN NEW.status IS NOT NEW.state BEGIN UPDATE work_orders SET status = NEW.state WHERE id = NEW.id; END
CREATE TRIGGER sync_insert AFTER INSERT ON work_orders BEGIN UPDATE work_orders SET state = COALESCE(NEW.state, NEW.status), status = COALESCE(NEW.state, NEW.status) WHERE id = NEW.id; END
